You are porting PyYAML to zero-dependency JavaScript ESM.

FIRST: read /workspace/spec/PORTING.md in full. It defines the hard constraints
(no RegExp, no JSON, no external imports, .mjs suffixes, never write a
backslash-u escape into a file), the mixin composition pattern, and the exact
API of the already-written foundation modules in /output/lib/
(chars.mjs, errors.mjs, pytypes.mjs, tokens.mjs, events.mjs, nodes.mjs).
Read those foundation files too — import from them, never duplicate them.

Ground truth is the reference binary. Run it to check behaviour whenever you are
unsure:  /workspace/dataset/test4_executable --a '<yaml text>'
It is PyYAML 6.0-era. Do NOT run python. Do NOT read or write any file outside
/output/lib except to read /workspace/spec/PORTING.md and /workspace/dataset/test4.py.

Port FAITHFULLY: same method decomposition as PyYAML, same control flow, same
error strings, same edge cases. This is a transcription task, not a redesign.
Every PyYAML regex must become an explicit character-scanning matcher; put the
original pattern in a comment above it.

Write ONLY the files assigned to you. Other agents are concurrently writing the
sibling modules; do not create, modify, or stub them. Assume every method listed
in the cross-module contract table in PORTING.md exists on 'this'.

When done, verify your file at least parses:
  node --input-type=module -e "import('/output/lib/YOURFILE.mjs').then(()=>console.log('ok'),e=>{console.error(e);process.exit(1)})"
(An import error naming a sibling module that does not exist yet is expected and
fine; a SyntaxError in your own file is not.)
Then self-check the constraints:
  grep -nE "require\(|module\.exports|JSON\.|new RegExp|\.match\(|\.matchAll\(" /output/lib/YOURFILE.mjs
  grep -n "u00\|u20\|u{" /output/lib/YOURFILE.mjs   # no backslash-u escapes
Fix anything that turns up.

Return a terse report: what you wrote, and any place you were unsure of PyYAML's
exact behaviour (those become follow-up checks).

Write /output/lib/reader.mjs (export ReaderMixin) and /output/lib/scanner.mjs
(export ScannerMixin) — ports of PyYAML's reader.py and scanner.py.

reader.mjs — the input is ALWAYS a JS string (the --a argument), so only
PyYAML's 'isinstance(stream, str)' branch matters:
- name = "<unicode string>".
- check_printable BEFORE buffering. PyYAML's NON_PRINTABLE pattern is
  [^\x09\x0A\x0D\x20-\x7E\x85\xA0-\uD7FF\uE000-\uFFFD\U00010000-\U0010ffff]
  i.e. reject anything not in that allowed set. On a hit raise
  ReaderError(name, position, character, 'unicode', "special characters are not allowed")
  where position is the code-point index of the offending character.
- buffer = the input PLUS a trailing '\0' sentinel, stored as an ARRAY OF
  SINGLE-CODE-POINT STRINGS (use [...text] so astral characters count as one,
  exactly like Python str indexing). index/line/column/pointer all count code
  points. Mark receives this array as its buffer.
- peek(i=0) returns buffer[pointer+i], or '\0' if that is past the end.
  prefix(n=1) returns the joined slice, clamped at the end.
  forward(n=1) advances, incrementing line and zeroing column on
  LF/NEL/LS/PS or on a CR not followed by LF, and incrementing column for any
  other character except the BOM.
  getMark() returns new Mark(name, index, line, column, buffer, pointer).

scanner.mjs — a complete port of PyYAML's Scanner: the tokens/indents/
possible_simple_keys machinery plus every method:
  checkToken/peekToken/getToken, needMoreTokens, fetchMoreTokens,
  nextPossibleSimpleKey, stalePossibleSimpleKeys, savePossibleSimpleKey,
  removePossibleSimpleKey, unwindIndent, addIndent,
  fetchStreamStart, fetchStreamEnd, fetchDirective, fetchDocumentStart,
  fetchDocumentEnd, fetchDocumentIndicator, fetchFlowSequenceStart,
  fetchFlowMappingStart, fetchFlowCollectionStart, fetchFlowSequenceEnd,
  fetchFlowMappingEnd, fetchFlowCollectionEnd, fetchFlowEntry,
  fetchBlockEntry, fetchKey, fetchValue, fetchAlias, fetchAnchor, fetchTag,
  fetchLiteral, fetchFolded, fetchBlockScalar, fetchSingle, fetchDouble,
  fetchFlowScalar, fetchPlain,
  checkDirective, checkDocumentStart, checkDocumentEnd, checkBlockEntry,
  checkKey, checkValue, checkPlain,
  scanToNextToken, scanDirective, scanDirectiveName, scanYamlDirectiveValue,
  scanYamlDirectiveNumber, scanTagDirectiveValue, scanTagDirectiveHandle,
  scanTagDirectivePrefix, scanDirectiveIgnoredLine, scanAnchor, scanTag,
  scanBlockScalar, scanBlockScalarIndicators, scanBlockScalarIgnoredLine,
  scanBlockScalarIndentation, scanBlockScalarBreaks, scanFlowScalar,
  scanFlowScalarNonSpaces, scanFlowScalarSpaces, scanFlowScalarBreaks,
  scanPlain, scanPlainSpaces, scanTagHandle, scanTagUri, scanUriEscapes,
  scanLineBreak.
Use SCAN_ESCAPES / SCAN_ESCAPE_CODES from chars.mjs for double-quoted escapes
(note PyYAML 5.4+ also accepts \/ — the table already includes it). scanUriEscapes
must decode percent-escaped UTF-8 byte sequences into characters.
Reproduce PyYAML's ScannerError messages verbatim, e.g.
 "while scanning for the next token" / "found character '@' that cannot start any token",
 "mapping values are not allowed here",
 "while scanning a block scalar" / "expected a comment or a line break, but found ...".

Behaviours to verify against the binary once you are done reasoning:
  '- 1'   '[1,2]'   'a: b'   '? k\n: v'   '|\n  x'   '>\n  x'   '"a\\tb"'
  '!!str x'   '&a x'   '*a'   '%YAML 1.1\n--- x'   'a: b\n c: d' (must error)

1	# Porting contract: PyYAML → JavaScript (ESM)
2	
3	We are reimplementing, from behaviour, the exact subset of PyYAML that this
4	Python program exercises:
5	
6	```python
7	result = yaml.dump(yaml.safe_load(args.a), default_flow_style=False)
8	print(result)
9	```
10	
11	Reference binary (ground truth, run it freely):
12	`/workspace/dataset/test4_executable --a '<yaml>'`
13	
14	It is PyYAML **6.0**-era behaviour (`\/` escape supported; timestamps keep
15	`tzinfo`; fractional seconds are truncated to 6 digits, never rounded).
16	`yaml.dump` uses the **full `Dumper`**, not `SafeDumper` — so `tuple` is
17	represented as `!!python/tuple`.
18	
19	## HARD CONSTRAINTS — a violation invalidates the whole deliverable
20	
21	1. **ESM only.** `import` / `export`. No `require`, no `module.exports`.
22	2. **`.mjs` suffix** on every file, and every relative import must spell the
23	   suffix: `import { x } from './chars.mjs'`.
24	3. **Zero external dependencies.** Only relative imports of our own files.
25	   No npm packages. No `node:` built-ins either, except that the entry point may
26	   use `node:process`-style globals (`process.argv`, `process.stdout`).
27	4. **No `RegExp`, ever.** No regex literals (`/.../`), no `new RegExp`, no
28	   `.match()` / `.matchAll()` / `.search()`, and no regex argument to
29	   `.replace()` / `.split()`. String arguments to `.replace()`, `.replaceAll()`,
30	   `.split()`, `.indexOf()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()` are fine. Every
31	   pattern PyYAML expresses as a regex must become an explicit character-by-
32	   character matcher function.
33	5. **No `JSON`.** Do not reference `JSON.parse`, `JSON.stringify`, or any other
34	   member of it, anywhere — not even in a comment or a debug line.
35	6. **Never write a `\uXXXX` escape into a source file.** The authoring pipeline
36	   decodes those into raw characters. Import the character you need from
37	   `./chars.mjs`, or build it with `String.fromCharCode(0xNNNN)`. `\n`, `\t`,
38	   `\r`, `\0`, `\xNN` escapes are safe to write.
39	7. **No Python.** Do not shell out to python, and do not embed Python source.
40	
41	## Style
42	
43	Terse, idiomatic modern JS. camelCase methods. Keep the port structurally
44	line-for-line with PyYAML so it can be audited against the original: same method
45	decomposition, same control flow, same error strings. Where a PyYAML regex
46	becomes a hand-rolled matcher, put the original pattern in a comment above it.
47	Comment density: sparse — only where the port diverges from PyYAML or where the
48	character-level logic is not self-evident.
49	
50	## Composition: mixins, not multiple inheritance
51	
52	PyYAML builds `Loader` and `Dumper` by multiple inheritance over mixin classes.
53	In JS each module exports a **mixin factory**:
54	
55	```js
56	export const ScannerMixin = (Base) => class extends Base { /* ... */ };
57	```
58	
59	`loader.mjs` / `dumper.mjs` (written by the integrator, not you) compose them:
60	
61	```js
62	class Root {}
63	const Loader = ResolverMixin(ConstructorMixin(ComposerMixin(
64	  ParserMixin(ScannerMixin(ReaderMixin(Root))))));
65	```
66	
67	Consequences you must respect:
68	
69	- All mixins share one `this`. Initialise your own state in the constructor
70	  after `super(...args)`. The constructor receives whatever `new Loader(text)`
71	  is called with — pass args through with `super(...args)`.
72	- You may freely call methods defined by *other* mixins on `this`
73	  (e.g. the scanner calls `this.getMark()`, the composer calls `this.resolve()`).
74	- Do not redefine a method another mixin owns.
75	
76	## Foundation modules (already written — import, do not modify)
77	
78	### `./chars.mjs`
79	Named characters and character sets, all built with `String.fromCharCode`:
80	`NUL BELL BACKSPACE TAB LF VTAB FF CR ESC SPACE NEL NBSP LS PS BOM`,
81	`LINE_BREAKS` (`\r\n` + NEL + LS + PS), `LINE_BREAKS_Z` (NUL + those),
82	`BLANK_Z` (NUL, space, tab, breaks), `SPACES` (` \t`), `BLANK` (spaces+breaks),
83	`DIGITS`, `HEX_DIGITS`, `LETTERS_DIGITS`, `ALPHA` (letters+digits+`-_`),
84	`EMIT_ESCAPES` (Map char → escape letter), `SCAN_ESCAPES` (Map letter → char),
85	`SCAN_ESCAPE_CODES` (Map of `x`→2, `u`→4, `U`→8).
86	
87	### `./errors.mjs`
88	- `Mark(name, index, line, column, buffer, pointer)` — `buffer` is an **array of
89	  single-code-point strings**; `pointer`/`index`/`column` are code-point counts.
90	  `toString()` reproduces PyYAML's `  in "<unicode string>", line N, column M:`
91	  plus snippet and caret.
92	- `YAMLError`, `MarkedYAMLError`, and the marked subclasses
93	  `ScannerError, ParserError, ComposerError, ConstructorError`, each constructed
94	  as `new ScannerError(context, contextMark, problem, problemMark, note?)`.
95	- `ReaderError(name, position, character, encoding, reason)`.
96	- `EmitterError(msg)`, `SerializerError(msg)`, `RepresenterError(msg)`.
97	- `PyValueError(msg)`, `PyTypeError(msg)` — stand-ins for the builtin Python
98	  exceptions PyYAML lets propagate. Every error carries `.qualifiedName`
99	  (e.g. `'yaml.scanner.ScannerError'`, `'ValueError'`) for the traceback printer.
100	
101	### `./pytypes.mjs`
102	Python value semantics. **Python `int` is `BigInt`; Python `float` is `number`.**
103	That distinction is load-bearing: `1` dumps as `1`, `1.0` dumps as `1.0`.
104	- `PyBytes{bytes: Uint8Array}`, `PyTuple{items: []}`, `PySet`, `PyDict`,
105	  `PyDate{year,month,day}`, `PyDateTime{...,tzOffsetMinutes}`.
106	- `PyDict`: insertion-ordered, Python key equality (`1`/`1.0`/`true` collide).
107	  `.set(k,v) .get(k) .has(k) .items() .keys() .size .update(other)`.
108	- `PySet`: `.add(v) .has(v) .values() .size`.
109	- `PyDate.isoformat()`, `PyDateTime.isoformat(sep)`.
110	- `pyKey(v)` — canonical hash key; throws `PyTypeError` for unhashable.
111	- `pyTypeName(v)` — `'int'`, `'str'`, `'dict'`, …
112	- `pyReprFloat(n)` — CPython `repr()` of a float (`1.0`, `1e+17`, `1e-05`).
113	- `pyLessThan(a,b)` — Python `<`, throwing `PyTypeError` on mixed types.
114	- `pyEquals(a,b)`.
115	- `pySortInPlace(items, less)` — CPython `list.sort()` comparison order.
116	- `encodeBase64Wrapped(bytes)` — `base64.encodebytes` (76-col wrap, trailing \n).
117	- `decodeBase64(text)` — `binascii.a2b_base64`.
118	
119	### `./tokens.mjs`
120	`StreamStartToken StreamEndToken DirectiveToken DocumentStartToken
121	DocumentEndToken BlockSequenceStartToken BlockMappingStartToken BlockEndToken
122	FlowSequenceStartToken FlowMappingStartToken FlowSequenceEndToken
123	FlowMappingEndToken KeyToken ValueToken BlockEntryToken FlowEntryToken
124	AliasToken AnchorToken TagToken ScalarToken`, plus `isToken(tok, ...classes)`.
125	
126	Positional constructor args mirror PyYAML: value fields first, then
127	`startMark, endMark`. So `new AnchorToken(value, startMark, endMark)`,
128	`new BlockEndToken(startMark, endMark)`,
129	`new ScalarToken(value, plain, startMark, endMark, style)`.
130	Every token has `.id` (`'<scalar>'`, `'['`, `':'`, …) — used verbatim in parser
131	error messages — and `.tokenType`.
132	
133	### `./events.mjs`
134	`StreamStartEvent(startMark, endMark, encoding)`,
135	`StreamEndEvent(startMark, endMark)`,
136	`DocumentStartEvent(startMark, endMark, explicit, version, tags)`,
137	`DocumentEndEvent(startMark, endMark, explicit)`,
138	`AliasEvent(anchor, startMark, endMark)`,
139	`ScalarEvent(anchor, tag, implicit, value, startMark, endMark, style)`,
140	`SequenceStartEvent(anchor, tag, implicit, startMark, endMark, flowStyle)`,
141	`SequenceEndEvent(startMark, endMark)`, `MappingStartEvent(...)` like sequence,
142	`MappingEndEvent(startMark, endMark)`.
143	Also exported for `instanceof` checks: `Event NodeEvent CollectionStartEvent
144	CollectionEndEvent`. Field names are camelCase: `flowStyle`, `startMark`.
145	
146	### `./nodes.mjs`
147	`ScalarNode(tag, value, startMark, endMark, style)`,
148	`SequenceNode(tag, value, startMark, endMark, flowStyle)`,
149	`MappingNode(...)`, base `Node`, `CollectionNode`. Each has `.nodeId`
150	(`'scalar' | 'sequence' | 'mapping'`).
151	
152	## Cross-module method contract (exact names — other agents call these)
153	
154	| Module | Mixin export | Methods other modules call |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| `reader.mjs` | `ReaderMixin` | `peek(i=0)`, `prefix(n=1)`, `forward(n=1)`, `getMark()`; fields `name index line column buffer pointer` |
157	| `scanner.mjs` | `ScannerMixin` | `checkToken(...classes)`, `peekToken()`, `getToken()` |
158	| `parser.mjs` | `ParserMixin` | `checkEvent(...classes)`, `peekEvent()`, `getEvent()` |
159	| `composer.mjs` | `ComposerMixin` | `checkNode()`, `getNode()`, `getSingleNode()` |
160	| `resolver.mjs` | `ResolverMixin` | `resolve(NodeClass, value, implicit)`, `descendResolver(currentNode, currentIndex)`, `ascendResolver()` |
161	| `constructor.mjs` | `ConstructorMixin` | `getSingleData()`, `constructDocument(node)`, `constructObject(node, deep=false)` |
162	| `emitter.mjs` | `EmitterMixin` | `emit(event)`; constructor reads options |
163	| `serializer.mjs` | `SerializerMixin` | `open()`, `serialize(node)`, `close()` |
164	| `representer.mjs` | `RepresenterMixin` | `represent(data)` |
165	
166	`resolve` takes the **node class itself** (`ScalarNode`/`SequenceNode`/
167	`MappingNode`), as PyYAML does, and `implicit` is a 2-element array
168	`[plainImplicit, nonPlainImplicit]`.
169

1	// Central table of the control / separator characters YAML cares about.
2	//
3	// Every one is built with String.fromCharCode rather than a "\u...." escape so
4	// that no raw U+0085 / U+2028 / U+2029 byte is ever embedded in a source file
5	// (a raw U+2028 inside a string literal is legal but hostile to tooling).
6	
7	export const NUL = String.fromCharCode(0x00);
8	export const BELL = String.fromCharCode(0x07);
9	export const BACKSPACE = String.fromCharCode(0x08);
10	export const TAB = String.fromCharCode(0x09);
11	export const LF = String.fromCharCode(0x0a);
12	export const VTAB = String.fromCharCode(0x0b);
13	export const FF = String.fromCharCode(0x0c);
14	export const CR = String.fromCharCode(0x0d);
15	export const ESC = String.fromCharCode(0x1b);
16	export const SPACE = String.fromCharCode(0x20);
17	export const NEL = String.fromCharCode(0x85);
18	export const NBSP = String.fromCharCode(0xa0);
19	export const LS = String.fromCharCode(0x2028);
20	export const PS = String.fromCharCode(0x2029);
21	export const BOM = String.fromCharCode(0xfeff);
22	
23	/** PyYAML's '\r\n\x85  ' — every character that ends a line. */
24	export const LINE_BREAKS = CR + LF + NEL + LS + PS;
25	
26	/** PyYAML's '\0\r\n\x85  ' — line breaks plus end-of-stream. */
27	export const LINE_BREAKS_Z = NUL + LINE_BREAKS;
28	
29	/** PyYAML's '\0 \t\r\n\x85  ' — whitespace, breaks and end-of-stream. */
30	export const BLANK_Z = NUL + SPACE + TAB + LINE_BREAKS;
31	
32	/** PyYAML's ' \t' */
33	export const SPACES = SPACE + TAB;
34	
35	/** PyYAML's ' \t\r\n\x85  ' */
36	export const BLANK = SPACES + LINE_BREAKS;
37	
38	export const DIGITS = '0123456789';
39	export const HEX_DIGITS = '0123456789ABCDEFabcdef';
40	export const LETTERS_DIGITS =
41	  '0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz';
42	/** Characters allowed in an alphanumeric-ish token body (anchors, tag handles). */
43	export const ALPHA = LETTERS_DIGITS + '-_';
44	
45	/** Emitter table: character -> the letter that follows the backslash. */
46	export const EMIT_ESCAPES = new Map([
47	  [NUL, '0'],
48	  [BELL, 'a'],
49	  [BACKSPACE, 'b'],
50	  [TAB, 't'],
51	  [LF, 'n'],
52	  [VTAB, 'v'],
53	  [FF, 'f'],
54	  [CR, 'r'],
55	  [ESC, 'e'],
56	  ['"', '"'],
57	  ['\\', '\\'],
58	  [NEL, 'N'],
59	  [NBSP, '_'],
60	  [LS, 'L'],
61	  [PS, 'P'],
62	]);
63	
64	/** Scanner table: the letter after a backslash -> the character it denotes. */
65	export const SCAN_ESCAPES = new Map([
66	  ['0', NUL],
67	  ['a', BELL],
68	  ['b', BACKSPACE],
69	  ['t', TAB],
70	  [TAB, TAB],
71	  ['n', LF],
72	  ['v', VTAB],
73	  ['f', FF],
